column1: # The engine's layout: one row per script under `tools/loop/`, the bound the suite compares its length against, the
# position the entry sources it at, and the functions it owns. Nothing is described twice — the file a behaviour
# lives in is a row a person can find, not prose a reviewer remembers (issue #890, issue #892).
# `driver#everyEngineScriptIsInTheTable` reads the file column against the scripts themselves in both directions,
# `driver#aCallToALaterFilesFunctionFails` read the order, and `driver#anOwnedFunctionIsInItsOwnersFile` reads the
# owner column against the definitions. A column is read by position, so the order below is the format: `file`,
# bound  the file's length when this row was written plus a quarter, rounded up: it records today's size and refuses
#        growth only, so raising one is a one-line diff with a reason beside it rather than a refactor.
# order  the position the entry sources the file at, or `-` when the entry does not source it. A file with an order
#        is part of the chain the entry loads: `lib.sh` first, then the file that records the evidence, then the
# owner  the functions the file defines, space separated, or `-` for a script that is an entry of its own — its
#        functions are words its own process runs and no other file may call. A function belongs to exactly one
#        file, so a definition in a file other than its owner's is a red case.
# note   why the row is what it is: the number a bound was raised from, or what the file holds.
